name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index near 102.2 on 11 Nov, up 2.6% over three months and just under its 52-week high
state: The DXY dollar index was near 102.2 early on 11 Nov, up 2.6% over three months and 0.7% on the week, just under its 52-week high of 102.6 (Yahoo Finance). That is inside the 5% three-month Watch line and the 90–108 range. SOFR was 2bp below the Fed's reserve rate on 9 Nov, showing no dollar funding strain (FRED).
for_you: A firmer dollar makes US goods, dollar-priced commodities and US travel dearer for people paid in pounds or euros.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 3.25% below the 5% Watch line
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
